$schema_note: AUTHORED, and deliberately small. It carries the Thompson plat's BLOCK NUMBERS for the blocks this reconstruction can reach them, and the numbering scheme inside a block, with the reading each rests on. Read by tools/generate_plat_lots.py, which stamps `plat_block_number` onto a block of data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json and `plat_lot_number` onto its lots. Nothing here authors geometry: a block's boundary and its lot lines are derived from the committed street lines exactly as before, and this file only puts a NUMBER on them.
why_this_file_exists: The most precise placement statement in the whole newspaper corpus is G. Spring's For-Sale notice — 'LOT No. 7, in block No. 16, one lot east of Haddock's Tavern, on Lake street' — and it resolved to nothing, because data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json keys its blocks on their bounding streets and no committed source numbered one. Three separate readings recorded that the address was the most placeable thing the corpus said and that placing it was somebody else's job (T-0324, and the June and October readings of the notice). This file is that job. T-0358. Rebuilt 2026-09-06 (T-0788, owner ask): the numerals are read off the georeferenced BPL scan, block by block, instead of counted along one tier from two of them.
grades: Each entry's `confidence` grades THE NUMBER ON THIS BLOCK, not the block. Nothing here is `documented`: a numeral read off a survey sheet is read at this dataset's own +/-20 m georeference, so even a numeral that fills its own block's crop carries an identification step the sheet does not make for us. `numeral_on_sheet` says which numbers are read and which are counted — twenty-two read, one counted (the Public Square, bracketed by read numerals on both sides) — so the difference does not vanish into one grade.

reading.asset_note: The BPL/Leventhal copy of J. S. Wright's 1834 survey — commonwealth:js957744g, 4204 x 5166 px — read through the IIIF image API at 6x on crops CUT TO EACH BLOCK'S OWN GROUND. This is the scan this project is georeferenced to (data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_gcps.json, affine fitted from eight ground control points, RMS 17.5 m), so a crop can be computed from a block's committed street lines rather than found by eye, and the numeral that falls inside it is the numeral on that block. The earlier reading used one 639 x 719 px crop of two blocks supplied by the owner (prefire_views_kevin_2026_08/wright1834_clark_reach_crop.jpeg); that crop's two numerals, 19 and 18, are both re-read here and both stand.
reading.method: For each block the grid holds, the four bounding street centrelines of data/streets/1835.json give a box in local ENU; tools/wright_px.py maps its corners into the BPL resource space; the box is padded 6 px and requested from IIIF at 6x. The block fills the frame, so the reading is an identification made by the committed georeference and not by counting from a neighbour. Every entry below cites the region it was read on, and any reader may re-open it and disagree.
reading.what_it_carries: Wright writes a numeral across the middle of every block of the Original Town. TWENTY-TWO of them fall on ground this project's street grid can address, and all twenty-two are read here: the South Water-Lake tier 21 20 19 18 17 16 west to east; the Lake-Randolph tier 28 29 west of the South Branch and 31 32 33 34 35 36 east of it; the Randolph-Washington tier 45 44 west of the branch, 43 42 41 40 east of it, then the block labelled 'Public Square' and no numeral, then 38 37. Lot numerals are printed inside several blocks; four of them are read in `lot_numbering` below.
reading.direction: THE RUN REVERSES TIER BY TIER, which is why it could never be counted from two numerals. Along South Water-Lake the number FALLS eastward (21 -> 16). Along Lake-Randolph it RISES eastward (31 -> 36). Along Randolph-Washington it FALLS again (43 -> 37). The refusal this file used to carry — that nothing said how the run passes from one tier to the next — was the right refusal: a boustrophedon is exactly what the sheet turns out to draw, and a run counted straight down the tiers would have numbered the Lake tier backwards.
reading.supersedes: The 2026-08-29 reading counted four of the six South Water numbers from the two it could read. All four are now read off the sheet and all four counted values were right: 21, 20, 17 and 16 stand as they were, and their grade changes from counted to read. Nothing moves.

identification.method: the watercourse in the street between the two blocks, which this project has already traced and committed
identification.note: docs/RESEARCH/clark_reach_bulge_1834.md § 4 measured the drawn watercourse's mouth at local E +462…+469 and established that the committed trace runs up the inside of its own ink line there — the stream is real, traced, and NOT the river bulge that memo was about. That places the street the stream runs down in the east half of the La Salle corridor. The nearest alternatives are Wells at E +329.3 (122 m west) and Clark at E +574.7 (123 m east), so the identification is unambiguous at this dataset's ±20 m working uncertainty even though it is an inference. The two blocks the crop numbers are therefore the Wells–La Salle block (19) and the La Salle–Clark block (18) of the tier fronting South Water Street on the north and Lake Street on the south.

lot_numbering.scheme: counter-clockwise from the block's north-east corner: lot 1 at the east end of the north row, running WEST to lot 4 at its west end; lot 5 at the west end of the south row, running EAST to lot 8 at its east end.
lot_numbering.read_from: FOUR blocks, in two tiers, all reading the same way: block 20 (blk_south_water_franklin), block 18 (blk_south_water_lasalle), block 16 (blk_south_water_dearborn) and block 40 (blk_randolph_wells). Each prints 4 3 2 1 across its north row west to east and 5 6 7 8 across its south row west to east. The scheme was read on block 18 alone in 2026-08-29, on a crop that cut the fourth lot off each row; three complete blocks now confirm it, including one in a different tier whose BLOCK numbering runs the other way — so the lot run is a property of the block and not of the tier.
lot_numbering.note: THE SCHEME IS NOW READ ON FOUR BLOCKS AND THE LINES IT NUMBERS ARE STILL NOT DRAWN FROM ANY SHEET. The lot lines in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json are the Thompson module divided into a block, graded `conjectural` for that reason, and a number put on a conjectural line is conjectural whatever the number's own provenance. What the four readings buy is the SCHEME, which is no longer a one-block reading; what they do not buy is the line. What the scheme is good for is reading a documented ADDRESS onto the grid, which is what it was fetched for.
lot_numbering.ten_lot_blocks: NOT EVERY BLOCK CARRIES EIGHT LOTS. The West Division block west of block 28 prints lot numerals 1 4 5 8 9 down its side — ten lots to the block, in two rows of five, with the numerals written across a horizontal alley rather than a vertical one. The module divides every block it builds into four lots per face and has no idea this shape exists. No West Division block is emitted by the generator today, so nothing is mis-numbered by it; recorded here so that the day one is, this is found first. The blocks the generator DOES emit are all in the eight-lot tiers, and all four blocks whose lot numerals are read above carry eight. CORRECTED 2026-09-13, T-0689. The count was right and the alley's bearing was not. Thompson's own sheet, read block by block across all six West Division tiers (data/traces/thompson_west_division_lots.json), draws the ten lots as TWO COLUMNS OF FIVE with the alley running NORTH-SOUTH between them — each lot 180 ft deep east-west, fronting the north-south street on the outer side of its column and backing on the alley. That is what 'numerals down its side' was already describing; 'a horizontal alley' in the same sentence was the slip. The sheet also refuses the other half of the assumption: the West Division lot fronts 75 3/5 ft, not the South Division's 80, and two of the six tiers carry EIGHT lots rather than ten. Still nothing is mis-numbered by the generator, which emits no West Division block; the correction is here so that the day it does, this is found first.
lot_numbering.emitted_for: only the blocks numbered above. A lot number without a block number says nothing.
lot_numbering.north_division: THE NORTH DIVISION TIER RUNS ITS ROWS THE OTHER WAY UP, and that is read, not assumed. Four of the seven blocks below print both rows legibly — blocks 7, 4, 2 and 1 — and every one of them prints 5 6 7 8 across its NORTH row west to east and 4 3 2 1 across its SOUTH row west to east. The three South Division tiers print the mirror of that (4 3 2 1 north, 5 6 7 8 south). So lot 1 sits at the block's south-east corner here and at its north-east corner there, and in both divisions the run begins on the row that faces the river. This file does NOT claim that river rule: it is one reading in each division, and a tier away from the water in either would test it. What is claimed is the four North Division blocks, which agree with one another.
lot_numbering.confidence_note_north: conjectural for the same reason as the scheme above — no North Division block has generated lot lines at all (tools/generate_plat_lots.py emits the South Division tiers only), so this is a scheme with nothing yet to number.

Every number here is `inferred` and not `documented`, even though twenty-two of the twenty-four are numerals read off a survey sheet. The number is read; WHICH BLOCK CARRIES IT is an identification made through this project's own affine fit, RMS 17.5 m against a 97 m block. The grade is the weaker of the two steps, as it was before.

None was consulted and none may be. Every number here comes off the survey sheet or, in the single case of the Public Square, off numerals read on both sides of it; if a reprint agrees that is a corroboration somebody may fetch and cite, and if it disagrees it is evidence, but neither may be substituted for this reading without saying so.

blocks_not_in_the_grid._doc: Numerals read on ground the generated grid has no id for, so they cannot be stamped onto a block without inventing one. They are kept here so the reading is not lost and so the next person to widen the grid finds the number already waiting. Nothing reads this section. T-1088 adds the North Division's whole Kinzie-to-the-river tier — seven numerals, 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 west to east — for this reason and no other: the tier's street control is committed and attested, so every crop below is cut from it by tools/read_north_division_numerals.py and re-cut by the gate, but tools/generate_plat_lots.py emits only the three South Division tiers, so there is no cell for the numbers to be stamped onto. Widen the generator and these seven are waiting. T-1094 adds the Original Town's southernmost tier — Washington Street to Madison Street, seven numerals, 52 53 54 55 56 57 58 rising eastward — on the same terms and with one stated weakness: Washington and Madison are committed across the whole tier, but the seven flanking north-south lines stop at y = -400 m and are CONTINUED SOUTH along their own bearing to cut the boxes. That continuation is a computation from committed endpoints and is not written into data/streets/1835.json, because a line this project has no control for should not be published as one. generate_plat_lots.py emits nothing south of Washington either, so these seven wait for a cell beside the North Division's. T-1095 adds the West Division's eighteen - 8 9 10 11 12 13, 22 23 24 25 26 27 and 46 47 48 49 50 51 - on the same terms and with its own stated weakness: `clinton` and `canal` are committed and carry four of the boxes outright, the tier lines are committed but clipped at east -320 m and are continued WEST along their own bearings, and the two flanks Jefferson Street and Des Plaines Street would give are instead `clinton` stepped one and two modules west, because both streets are refused in docs/RESEARCH/west_division_streets.md section 2 for standing wholly west of the modelled ground. That step is corroborated three ways - it reproduces the committed `canal` to 0.46 m at Lake Street and 2.34 m at the scene's south edge, and lands 8.7 m and 8.2 m west of the two surviving intersections T-0446 committed in `fulton`'s note - and nothing is written into data/streets/1835.json by it. tools/read_west_division_numerals.py cuts every box and the gate re-cuts them, and it also asserts the boustrophedon ACROSS the blocks other tickets already read: 26 27 joins T-0788's 28 29 rising eastward, 47 46 joins its 45 44 43 falling eastward, and 48 49 50 51 runs on into T-1094's 52. generate_plat_lots.py emits nothing west of the river, so these eighteen wait for a cell with the other fourteen.
